content.text: dynamite: 3100 discussion posts from a virtual class forum, embedded + HDBSCAN min_cluster_size=15 -> 41 clusters + noise. i want an llm to name each cluster. i'll pass ~20 sample posts per cluster. write the prompt. output must be json

```text
You are labeling clusters of student discussion posts from an online course forum.

You will receive the posts for ONE cluster. Read them and return a JSON object:

{
  "label": "<3-6 word name for what these posts have in common>",
  "description": "<one sentence, concrete, mentions the course concept or activity>",
  "kind": "<one of: concept_question | logistics | debugging | opinion | social | resource_sharing | other>",
  "confidence": <0.0-1.0, how coherent the cluster looks>,
  "outliers": [<indices of posts that don't fit the label>]
}

Rules:
- Name the shared topic, not the tone ("Recursion base case confusion", not "Confused students").
- Use the course's own terms when posts use them.
- If posts share no clear topic, set label to "Mixed" and confidence below 0.4.
- Return only the JSON object, no other text.

Posts (index: text):
{posts}
```

Notes:
- Ask for `outliers` so you can see when HDBSCAN merged two topics; a cluster with 6+ outliers out of 20 is probably two clusters.
- Sample the 20 posts closest to the cluster centroid plus 5 random members, otherwise you only ever see the "cleanest" posts and the label looks better than the cluster is.
how do i check the labels are actually good without reading 3100 posts

You don't need to read everything:

1. **Hand-check all 41 labels against 10 random posts each** (410 posts, maybe 2 hours). Mark each label correct / partly / wrong.
2. **Intrusion test** for a subset: show yourself 5 posts from cluster A plus 1 from cluster B, see if you can spot the intruder using only the label. If you can't, the labels aren't discriminative.
3. **Track the `confidence` field against your hand check.** If low-confidence labels are the ones you marked wrong, you can use it to triage future runs.

Report it as "41 LLM-generated labels, each checked by hand against 10 random members; N revised."
did it. 6 relabeled, 2 merged (were the same topic, "midterm logistics" twice). so 40 clusters now? or keep 41

If you merged two clusters into one label, it's 40 topics. Whether you also merge them in the data depends on what you report:

- If you report **topics**, merge them → 40.
- If you report **HDBSCAN output**, keep 41 clusters and note that two map to one topic.

Most honest: "HDBSCAN produced 41 clusters; after manual review, two were the same topic, giving 40 topics. Six labels were revised."
